humanities_role_explanation: Designed to measure art-critical and cultural interpretation competence (L1-L5 grounded in Panofsky's iconology) on museum artworks from eight traditions; items target disciplinary art-historical competence, not generic ability.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Artwork images from museum collections paired with expert-written bilingual (Chinese-English) critiques; VLMs receive the image and generate an English critique, which is scored against culture-specific dimension sets.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Generative art critique spanning L1 visual perception, L2 technical analysis, L3 cultural symbolism (iconography), L4 historical context (period, artist, provenance, 'art-historical attribution'), and L5 philosophical aesthetics (iconological interpretation). Scored by Dimension Coverage Rate over 225 culture-specific dimensions.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to multicultural art critique with VLMs; a single-domain benchmark.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: GPT-4o, Claude-Sonnet-4.5, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Qwen3-VL-235B, GLM-4V-Flash; few-shot also DeepSeek-VL2 and Claude-Opus-4.5.

quantitative_metrics.note: Dimension Coverage Rate (keyword matching), layer gap ΔL, Spearman rank correlation, Cohen's kappa, ICC.

summary: VULCA-BENCH is a multicultural art-critique benchmark of 7,410 image-critique pairs across eight traditions with expert bilingual critiques annotated against a five-layer (L1-L5) framework with 225 culture-specific dimensions. A pilot of five VLMs shows a 31-40 point drop in dimension coverage from visual/technical (L1-L2) to cultural interpretation (L3-L5).
key_findings: All five models show a 31-40 pp drop from L1-L2 to L3-L5 (e.g., Gemini-2.5-Pro 89.2 vs 58.1; GPT-4o 87.1 vs 46.8). Gemini-2.5-Pro best with DCR 72.4. Naive few-shot prompting reduces DCR for most models (DeepSeek-VL2 -41.3%, GPT-4o -15.5%), while Claude models remain stable. Error patterns: surface terminology, anachronism, cultural conflation.
facets_explanation: Critiques were written by native expert annotators (PhD-level art historians) per tradition, following L1-L5 with explicit covered_dimensions labels, reviewed by a second expert. Each culture adapts the framework to its own aesthetic theory (e.g., rasa, wabi-sabi, qiyun), so correctness is culture-relative. Scoring checks which dimensions from a set are covered (keyword matching), and annotator disagreement is resolved by discussion/escalation and reported as IAA kappa.
results_explanation: Table 7 reports Gemini-2.5-Pro DCR 72.4 as best, with L1-L2 89.2 vs L3-L5 58.1 (ΔL 31.1); GPT-4o has the largest ΔL of 40.3, so the depth gap upper bound is 40 points (L1-L2 vs L3-L5). Few-shot (Appendix J) is an input comparison: DeepSeek-VL2 0.985 to 0.578 DCR. The headline metric is Dimension Coverage Rate, which is mapped to 'other'. The paper reports no human baseline score on the same metric; human IAA is reported but not compared against models. The evaluation set is N=336 balanced-pilot pairs; per-culture differences are not framed as a systematic asymmetry.

humanities_role.quote: a multicultural art-critique benchmark for evaluating Vision–Language Models’ (VLMs) cultural understanding beyond surface-level visual perception

dataset_size.quote: VULCA-BENCH comprises 7,410 matched image-critique pairs drawn from 11,964 total images

evaluation_set_size.quote: We sample 48 pairs per culture (N=336 total) and evaluate 5 VLMs

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: We compare zero-shot, 1-shot, and 3-shot prompting with DeepSeek-VL2, GPT-4o, Claude-Opus-4.5, and Claude-Sonnet-4.5

gold_source.quote: Expert annotators generate critiques following the L1–L5 framework.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: L1–L2 require visual observation; L3–L5 demand progressively deeper cultural knowledge that VLMs typically lack.

gold_community_dependent.quote: Framework symmetry ensures each culture adapts L1–L5 to its own aesthetic theory

answer_multiplicity.quote: Dc k ⊆Dk denotes the sub-set of dimensions detected via keyword matching.

plurality_treatment.quote: Annotator-reviewer disagreements are resolved through discussion with reference to authoritative sources; unresolved cases (<2%) escalate to senior expert panel.
